app.title: Cash Before You Bid
app.lede: Deposit, stamp duty, government fees, LMI, inspections, moving and a repayment buffer — everything you need in the bank before you sign, with the maths shown line by line.
app.metaDescription: Know your numbers before the auction starts: stamp duty, deposit, fees, and total upfront cash for your property purchase.

routes.htb: Help to Buy (2% deposit, government equity)

hints.scheme: The contract sets the deposit you pay on the day, usually 10%. The scheme needs at least 5%.
hints.htb: The contract sets the deposit you pay on the day, usually 10%. Help to Buy needs at least 2%.
hints.nolmi: The contract sets the deposit you pay on the day, usually 10%. 20% avoids LMI without a guarantor.
hints.lmi: The contract sets the deposit you pay on the day, usually 10%. Under 20%, LMI is charged.

cliffs.label: First home buyer duty thresholds
cliffs.exemptionBody: Up to {{price}} an eligible first home buyer pays no land transfer duty at all. Past it the exemption is gone and duty phases in, rising far more steeply with price than it does anywhere else.
cliffs.concessionBody: Between {{from}} and {{price}} the duty is scaled by how far into the band the price sits, climbing from nothing to the full amount across it. From {{price}} the concession is gone and the full duty applies.

privacy.claim: Your figures never leave your browser.
privacy.localBody: The whole calculation happens on this device, inside this page. There is no account, no sign-up, no tracking, no analytics and no lead capture — nothing you type is sent to us, to a broker, or to anyone else.
privacy.linkTerm: A link you share carries your numbers.
privacy.linkBody: Your figures sit in the address bar so the page can be reloaded and shared, which means anyone you send the link to can read them — your savings and pre-approved loan included — and a chat app or browser sync may keep a copy.
privacy.storageTerm: Saved scenarios stay on this device.
privacy.storageBody: Saving one keeps its numbers in this browser’s own storage, on this device only. They are never uploaded, and deleting one here deletes it everywhere.
privacy.thirdPartyTerm: One thing is loaded from elsewhere, and only if you ask.
privacy.thirdPartyBody: Every file this page needs — its code, its styling, even its fonts — is served from this site's own address, so no one else sees you arrive. The single exception is the exchange rate: switching the display to đồng fetches today's rate from exchangerate-api.com — the request your browser will show is to open.er-api.com — and nothing is fetched before you do. That request carries none of your figures, no cookie, and not even the address of the page you are on. Nothing else is added without this statement changing first.

money.disclaimer: Every figure above is an estimate, rounded to the nearest {{unit}}.
money.disclaimerSmall: Amounts under {{threshold}} are rounded to the nearest {{smallUnit}}.
money.roundingNote: Parts may not add to the total due to rounding.

currency.label: Currency
currency.note: Amounts are entered and calculated in Australian dollars; {{currency}} is a display conversion. The rate is fetched from {{provider}} the first time you switch — none of your figures are sent.

flags.schemeNotNeeded: With 20% or more you do not need the scheme; LMI is not charged anyway.
flags.schemeCapExceeded: Price is above the 5% Deposit Scheme cap of {{cap}} for this region — the scheme is not available; LMI has been applied instead.
flags.schemeResidency: The scheme requires an Australian citizen or permanent resident — LMI applied instead.
flags.schemeOwnerOccupier: The scheme is owner-occupier only — LMI applied instead.
flags.htbCapExceeded: Price is above the Help to Buy cap of {{cap}} for this region.
flags.htbCitizenship: Help to Buy requires Australian citizenship.
flags.htbDetails: Help to Buy: income caps {{single}} single / {{couple}} couple; 10,000 places a year; CBA and Bank Australia only (Jun 2026). Government share is {{share}} and is repaid at market value on sale.
flags.guarantorGap: Under 20% deposit without LMI needs a family guarantor pledging the gap; shown with no LMI.
flags.fhbResidency: The first home buyer duty exemption and concession require an Australian citizen or permanent resident — duty charged at the standard rates instead.
flags.fhogPriceCap: First Home Owner Grant not available: price above {{cap}}.
flags.genuineSavings: LVR above 90%: most lenders want 5% of the price as genuine savings held for 3+ months.
flags.serviceability: Serviceability check: the lender will test {{assessed}}/month at {{rate}}. If that is more than about 35–40% of your after-tax income, expect the loan to be cut.
flags.financeUnconditional: An auction contract is unconditional: there is no finance clause and no cooling-off period. A pre-approval is not the loan — if it does not settle you have defaulted on the contract, not merely missed out on the property, and the deposit is at risk.
flags.noPreApproval: No pre-approved loan amount entered, so the finance check has not been run — this is not the same as passing it. An auction contract is unconditional: there is no finance clause and no cooling-off period, so unconditional approval before you bid is what protects your deposit.

sunk.heading: Spent before the hammer falls
sunk.perPropertySub: Inspection and conveyancing, paid to go after one property. Your conveyancing figure also covers settlement work, which you pay for once — so this reads high.
sunk.searchSub_one: {{properties}} property, so nothing beyond the figure above
sunk.searchSub_other: {{properties}} × {{perProperty}} — {{lost}} of it on the ones you do not win
sunk.framing: This is the money that is gone whether you win or lose. The deposit, stamp duty, government fees, LMI and settlement costs above are only ever paid on the property you actually buy — these are not.
sunk.researchBefore: Consumer Policy Research Centre research, cited by the Victorian Government in March 2026, found building and pest reports cost $500–$600 for the pair, that about half of buyers paid for several inspections while house-hunting, and that 17% paid for seven or more — spending up to $4,200. The figures above are your own, not that research. Source:

bands.auctionDayNote: Due the moment the hammer falls
bands.atSettlementNote: Due weeks later, on the settlement date
bands.afterSettlementNote: Not needed on the day, but still money you have to have

verdicts.auctionDayCovered: Your savings cover the {{required}} deposit due the moment the hammer falls.
verdicts.auctionDayShort: Short {{shortfall}} for the {{required}} deposit due the moment the hammer falls.
verdicts.atSettlementCovered: What is left of your savings covers the {{required}} due at settlement, and your pre-approval covers the balance of the price.
verdicts.atSettlementCoveredCashOnly: What is left of your savings covers the {{required}} due at settlement.
verdicts.atSettlementShortMultiple: Short at settlement in both pockets. The cash gap and the loan gap are separate problems — a bigger pre-approval does not pay duty, and more savings do not enlarge the loan.
verdicts.shortAuctionDayCash: Cash: short {{shortfall}}. The deposit is {{required}} and you have {{available}}. Save more, or bid less.
verdicts.shortSettlementCash: Cash: short {{shortfall}}. Settlement needs {{required}} and {{available}} is left after the deposit. A loan does not fund duty and fees — this gap has to be cash.
verdicts.shortSettlementLoan: Loan: short {{shortfall}}. The balance of the price is {{required}} and your pre-approval is {{available}}. Ask your lender for more, or bid less.
verdicts.financeNotChecked: Finance not checked: no pre-approved loan amount entered. The balance of the price still has to come from somewhere.

safeMaxBid.heading: How high can you go?
safeMaxBid.label: Safe maximum bid
safeMaxBid.bound: Bid up to this and you can still pay the deposit when the hammer falls and everything due at settlement.
safeMaxBid.boundCash: Bid up to this and you can still pay the deposit when the hammer falls and everything due at settlement. Cash is what stops you here — every extra dollar you save raises it.
safeMaxBid.boundLoan: Bid up to this and you can still pay the deposit when the hammer falls and everything due at settlement. Your pre-approval is what stops you here — only a larger loan raises it.
safeMaxBid.boundBoth: Bid up to this and you can still pay the deposit when the hammer falls and everything due at settlement. Your cash and your pre-approval run out together, so raising one alone will not move it.
safeMaxBid.rounding: Rounded down to the nearest {{unit}}, so it is a figure you can call out. It assumes every other number on this page stays as it is.
safeMaxBid.noFigures: Enter your savings — and your pre-approved loan, once you have one — and this becomes the highest price you can call out and still settle.
safeMaxBid.unaffordable: There is no price you can cover yet: the costs that do not change with the price already come to more than your savings. The verdict below says by how much.
safeMaxBid.unbounded: Nothing in your figures caps a bid below {{price}}, the highest price this calculator takes.

guidance.auctionDay: Paying the deposit on the day
guidance.hammerTerm: Due on the fall of the hammer.
guidance.hammerBody: You sign the contract straight after the auction, and the deposit is payable then. An auction purchase has no cooling-off period.
guidance.percentTerm: The contract sets the percentage, not you.
guidance.percentBody: It is usually 10%. A 5% deposit does happen, but the vendor has to agree to it before the auction — check the contract of sale.
guidance.formTerm: Confirm the accepted forms with the agent beforehand.
guidance.formBody: Personal cheques are often not accepted. Typically it is a bank cheque, EFT, or the agent’s online deposit service.
guidance.bondTerm: Deposit bonds are rarely accepted in Victoria.
guidance.bondBody: Section 27 of the Sale of Land Act 1962 lets a vendor seek early release of a cash deposit, and a bond cannot be released that way — so a bond needs the vendor’s written agreement before the auction.
guidance.confirmBody: Terms vary from contract to contract: check yours with the agent and your conveyancer before you bid.

how.dutyFhbExempt: First home buyer exemption: dutiable value {{dutiableValue}} ≤ {{cap}} → {{zero}}
how.lmiScheme: 5% Deposit Scheme: government guarantees 15%, no LMI
how.lmiGuarantor: Guarantor covers the gap: no LMI
how.lmiChargedCapitalised: Loan {{loan}} × {{rate}} (LVR {{lvr}}) × 1.10 Victorian insurance duty — indicative — capitalised into the loan
how.conveyancing: Your figure: contract review and settlement work, committed before you bid.
how.settlementAdjustments: Rates, water, owners corp apportioned to settlement day
how.grant: New home ≤ {{cap}}, eligible first home buyer; usually applied at settlement
how.costsSubtotal: Sum of the lines above (excluding deposit)

notes.heading: Notes on the rules used
notes.dutyBody: (Victoria, general rates): 1.4% to $25k; $350 + 2.4% to $130k; $2,870 + 6% of the excess over $130k to $960k; 5.5% flat to $2m; $110,000 + 6.5% above. Owner-occupiers ≤ $550k use the PPR rates ($2,870 + 5% over $130k to $440k; $18,370 + 6% over $440k). First home buyers: $0 to $600k, then general duty × (value − $600k) ÷ $150k up to $750k. Off-the-plan: dutiable value = price − construction still to be built (temporary all-buyer version for strata contracts to 20 Apr 2027). Foreign purchasers +8%.
notes.feesBody: (Land Services Victoria 2026-27, PEXA FY27): transfer $104.30 + $2.34 per whole $1,000, capped at $3,614, rounded up; mortgage registration $129.20; PEXA transfer $146.30 and mortgage $74.14.
notes.lmiBody: : indicative, interpolated from Helia-derived tables — about 0.4% of the loan at 81% LVR, 1.2% at 85%, 2.25% at 90%, 4.0% at 95% — plus 10% Victorian insurance duty. Get a real quote; lenders and insurers differ.
notes.schemeBody: : no LMI; deposit 5–19.99%; price cap $950k Melbourne/Geelong, $650k elsewhere; owner-occupier citizens/PRs.
notes.htbBody: : 2% minimum deposit; government equity 30% existing / 40% new; income caps $103k single / $165k couple; citizens only; same price caps.
notes.grantBody: : $10,000, new homes ≤ $750k, first home buyers; usually paid at settlement through the lender, so it is shown here as reducing the cash you need.
notes.repaymentBody: : principal and interest over 30 years at your rate; the lender assesses you at your rate + 3 percentage points (APRA). Buffer = months × repayment at your rate + $1,000.
notes.ratesAsAtBefore: Rates current as at {{date}}. Check any figure with the
